steps.label: Write each reciprocal square
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. r = Δ/s inverts to 1/r = s/Δ, so 1/r² = s²/Δ² — and the ex-radii follow the same pattern with s−a, s−b, s−c.
steps.memory_tip: r = Δ/s inverts to 1/r = s/Δ, so 1/r² = s²/Δ². The ex-radii follow with s−a, s−b, s−c.
lines: (r = Δ/s, r₁ = Δ/(s−a), and so on;

recall.must_convey: That 1/r = s/Δ and 1/r₁ = (s−a)/Δ, so all four squares go over the common denominator Δ².
accept: one over r is s over delta so its square is s squared over delta squared and the others follow with s minus a
invert each radius and square, everything is over delta squared
all four terms share delta squared underneath
prathi radius invert chesi square cheyyali, delta square meeda vasthai
write the four reciprocal squares over delta squared

steps.why: Inverting and squaring can be done in either order; both give 1/r² = s²/Δ² at once.

steps.label: Expand and cancel
steps.margin_note: The other half. Expand the three brackets; the s² terms give 4s², the cross terms give −2s(a+b+c) = −4s², and those cancel exactly.
steps.memory_tip: The s² terms give 4s² and the cross terms give −2s(2s) = −4s² — they cancel exactly.

lines.text: ((s − a)² = s² − 2as + a², and so on)
(collect: 4s², then the −2s terms, then the squares)
= \ \dfrac{4s^{2}\ - \ 2s\left(2s\right)\ + \ a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}}{\Delta ^{2}}\left[\because \ a + b + c\ = \ 2s\right]

recall.must_convey: That expanding gives 4s² − 2s(a+b+c) + a²+b²+c², and that 4s² − 4s² cancels to leave (a²+b²+c²)/Δ².
accept: expand the brackets, four s squared minus two s times two s cancels leaving the sum of the squares over delta squared
the s squared terms cancel exactly
the answer is a squared plus b squared plus c squared over delta squared

steps.why: a + b + c = 2s is what makes 2s(a+b+c) equal 4s² — exactly the s² total from the four squares. Without that substitution nothing cancels.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the s² from the first term and getting 3s².

lines_compact.text: = \ \dfrac{4s^{2}\ - \ 2s\left(2s\right)\ + \ a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}}{\Delta ^{2}}\left[\because \ a + b + c\ = \ 2s\right]

insider_note: Write each reciprocal over Δ so the whole sum becomes one fraction. Expanding gives 4s² − 2s(a+b+c), and a + b + c = 2s makes those two terms cancel exactly.
